newsitem.title: UK: Sears has poor Christmas, warns on profits.
newsitem.headline: Sears has poor Christmas, warns on profits.

text.p: Troubled British retailer Sears Plc said on Thursday that it expected full year pretax profits before one-off items to be "significantly below last year's figure" of 100.1 million pounds.

The company, which brought forward its trading statement after newspaper reports it would make a profit warning, said same store sales in the Christmas period were down by 0.5 percent against a year ago but were up one percent in its second half to January 6.
Sears added that it would make an announcement "shortly" on talks with privately-owned retailing and pools group Littlewoods over the sale of its mail order business Freemans.
Shares extended losses to be down 5.5 pence at 86 pence by 1307 GMT after falling 3.5 pence in early trading.
Sears has struggled to show progress in turning around its sprawling retail business under the hand of chief executive Liam Strong, who took over around five years ago.

Its efforts to ditch part of its British Shoe business were hampered last year when stores sold to retailer Facia had to be taken back after Facia collapsed in June and Sears reportedly has a claim of some 30 million pounds against the group.
